{"decision":"NOT SETTLED, AND IT IS A FEATURE REQUEST RATHER THAN A DEFECT. Restated 2026-09-13 by flo2 after it withdrew the finding this was first raised as:

  ▎ Not a design-vs-code defect — reflow2's interface says internal and the code agrees.
  ▎ The question is whether to expose a selector at all, because without one flo2 cannot
  ▎ evaluate in-memory against the store, and that gates an open question on flo2's side.
  ▎ Your call whether it's worth it.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY, read from reflow2's source by flo2 rather than inferred from a fact about another project: KvBackend, MemoryBackend and RocksBackend are all pub(crate); selection is by which constructor runs; rocksdb is an optional Cargo feature whose ABSENCE MAKES open_rocksdb FAIL LOUD; and the CLI takes --graph-path and nothing naming a backend. Evaluating one backend against the other therefore means building a second binary.

⭐ THE FAIL-LOUD PROPERTY IS A CONSTRAINT ON ANY ANSWER, not a detail. A build without the feature refuses rather than quietly opening an empty design. A runtime selector must preserve that: "which backend is this design in" becoming a property of how the server was launched is exactly how a design opened under the wrong backend would present as EMPTY — the silent failure mode dec:one-process-many-stores already names for identity. Whatever shape this takes has to survive it.

WHAT IS ALREADY RULED, and it bears on this without answering it: dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds was REJECTED 2026-09-11 — RocksDB stays, because an engine swap forces a migration on every consumer to save build time on the builder's machine. That rejection was about REPLACING the engine. This asks whether both may be reachable from one binary, which is a different question and is not foreclosed by it.

THE COST TO WEIGH: one consumer, with one open question, against a new launch-time axis on a product whose whole premise is that a design lives in a directory and travels with the repo. Reflow2 has said no to smaller things for less reason. This is @ajs's call and is recorded so it can be declined on the record rather than drifting.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — is the byte backend selectable at RUNTIME, or does choosing it stay a compile-time act?","rationale":"Raised by @ajs from flo2's 2026-09-13 session, initially supported by a citation of fact:the-storage-seam-is-published-in-design-and-private-in-code as reflow2's own record of a design-vs-code mismatch. The misreading is recorded as fact:the-retired-dependency-fact-misled-a-second-reader-2026-09-13.
